days.title: When Spouses Disagree
days.question: If serious problems arise between husband and wife, what does Islam say to do? And when is divorce or khul' appropriate?
days.principle: When a wife's defiance (nushuz) is feared, it is prescribed to admonish her, then to stay away from her bed, then to strike her lightly without causing harm. If the matter worsens and a breakdown is feared, recourse is to arbitration, with an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers. Dissolving the marriage when it cannot be sustained is something Allah and His Messenger legislated, through divorce or khul'.

misconception.peopleSay: Since Allah mentioned striking, a man can hit his wife however he wants.
misconception.correct: The striking meant is a light disciplinary tap that does not break a bone or disfigure a limb. Ibn 'Abbas was asked about it and said: with a siwak (tooth-stick) and the like. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never struck a woman or a servant with his hand, and he made clear that those who hit their wives are not the best of Muslims.

days.action: If there is a disagreement in your home or with someone close to you, think of the Quranic solution: talking and advice first, and if the matter grows, a wise arbiter from each side's family who intends reconciliation.
lesson: The book establishes that obedience in the home is limited to what is not sinful; the Prophet ﷺ refused to let a woman obey her husband in adding hair extensions to her daughter's hair because it is haram. If defiance is feared, meaning the wife disobeys and holds herself above her husband's rights, the remedy is in order: admonition, then staying away from her bed, then a light strike that does not harm, with a siwak or the like. The book stresses that the Prophet ﷺ never struck a woman or a servant with his hand, and that those who hit their wives are not the best of Muslims. If the problem grows and a breakdown is feared, an arbiter from the husband's family and one from the wife's family are sent, and if they intend reconciliation, Allah will bring the two together. If life together becomes impossible, Allah legislated divorce by the husband or khul' by the wife, and divorce according to the Sunnah is in a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her.
days.quote: It is worth mentioning here that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never struck a woman or a servant with his hand.

quiz.question: A husband hits his wife hard, hurting her. Is this from the Shariah?
options: No, the striking mentioned is light, like with a siwak, and the Prophet ﷺ never struck a woman
quiz.explanation: Ibn 'Abbas was asked: What is striking that does not harm? He said: with a siwak and the like.

quiz.question: A serious disagreement between spouses that they cannot resolve. What does the Shariah say?
options: An arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers, to reconcile or separate
The stronger one imposes his view
quiz.explanation: When a breakdown between spouses is feared, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, legislated sending an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers, to reconcile or to separate.

quiz.question: A woman asked for divorce without any reason. What is the ruling?
quiz.explanation: It is forbidden for a wife to ask for divorce without a valid reason.

askTheBook: What are the steps for dealing with defiance in Islam?
What is arbitration between spouses?
What is the difference between divorce and khul'?

days.title: Divorce and the Waiting Period, and the Hijab
days.question: How many times can divorce happen? How long is the waiting period ('iddah)? And what does the book say about a woman's hijab?
days.principle: Divorce is twice, in which the husband has the right to take his wife back as long as she is in her waiting period; if he divorces her a third time, she is not lawful for him until she marries another husband. The waiting period for those who menstruate is three menstrual cycles, for those past menopause and those who have not menstruated three months, for pregnant women until they give birth, and for a woman whose husband has died four months and ten days.

misconception.peopleSay: Divorce can happen at any time and in any way; there's no such thing as divorce according to the Sunnah.
misconception.correct: Divorce according to the Sunnah is to divorce her while she is pure, without intercourse, and to have two witnesses. It is authentically reported from Ibn Mas'ud, on the verse «فطلقوهن لعدتهن», that he said: in a period of purity without intercourse.

days.action: Read the verse ﴿ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِۖ فَإِمْسَاكٌۢ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌۢ بِإِحْسَٰنٍ﴾ (al-Baqarah 229) and think about how Islam requires kindness and goodness even at the time of separation.
lesson: The book warns a wife against asking for divorce without a reason; the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever does so, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her. Divorce according to the Sunnah is in a period of purity in which there was no intercourse, with two witnesses. Divorce is twice, during which the husband can take his wife back as long as she is in her waiting period; if he divorces her a third time, she is not lawful for him until she marries someone else. The waiting period is three menstrual cycles for one who menstruates, three months for one past menopause or who has not yet menstruated, until giving birth for a pregnant woman, and four months and ten days for one whose husband has died. Then the book talks about a woman's hijab: Allah commanded the believing women to draw their outer garments over themselves and to draw their head-coverings over their chests, and not to display their adornment except what appears of it, with disagreement among scholars. It also forbade a woman from imitating men and forbade men from imitating women.
days.quote: With disagreement among the scholars about this exception, though the view that covering the face is obligatory has stronger evidence and is further from occasions of temptation.

quiz.question: A woman's husband died. How long is her waiting period?
quiz.explanation: As for the woman whose husband has died, her waiting period is four months and ten days.

quiz.question: When is divorce according to the Sunnah?
options: In a period of purity without intercourse
quiz.explanation: That he said: in a period of purity without intercourse.

quiz.question: A woman dresses and behaves like men. What is the ruling?
options: Forbidden, just as men are forbidden from imitating women
quiz.explanation: And that he forbade women from imitating men, just as he forbade men from imitating women.

days.title: Maintaining Ties of Kinship
days.question: If my relatives cut me off, should I stop keeping in touch with them too?
days.principle: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded maintaining the ties of kinship and mutual support among relatives, and made cutting off kinship one of the major sins that anger Allah and His Messenger.

misconception.peopleSay: Maintaining kinship means I visit only those who visit me, and whoever cuts me off, I cut him off.
misconception.correct: «ليس الواصل بالمكافئ، ولكن الواصل الذي إذا قطعت رحمه وصلها». And whoever keeps ties with his relatives while they cut him off will continue to have a supporter from Allah against them as long as he does so.

days.action: Call a relative today whom you haven't spoken to in a while, especially if he is the one who has fallen short with you, and remember: «ليس الواصل بالمكافئ».
lesson: Allah commanded maintaining the ties of kinship and paired it with fearing Him at the start of Surat an-Nisa', and made cutting off kinship a major sin. Kinship includes all your relatives, near and distant, but the closer they are, the more right they have to your kindness. The Prophet ﷺ made maintaining kinship one of the landmarks of Islam alongside tawhid, prayer and zakah, and even Abu Sufyan, while still a polytheist, knew that the Prophet ﷺ commanded maintaining ties. Allah said to kinship that He will keep ties with whoever keeps ties with it and cut off whoever cuts it off. Whoever wants Allah to expand his provision and bless his life should maintain his ties of kinship. The one who truly maintains ties is not the one who returns a visit with a visit, but the one who keeps ties with his relatives when they cut him off.
days.quote: Kin (arham) are relatives: those between whom there is a blood relationship, whether or not one inherits from the other, and whether or not they are mahram.

quiz.question: Your relative cuts you off while you keep visiting him. Do you keep visiting?
options: No, treat him the same way
Visit him once every few years
Yes, the one who truly maintains ties is the one who keeps ties with whoever cut him off

quiz.question: Who are one's kin?
options: Only those who inherit from you
Relatives with whom you share a blood relationship, even if they are not heirs
quiz.explanation: Kin are relatives: those between whom there is a blood relationship, whether or not one inherits from the other.

quiz.question: What is the ruling on cutting off kinship?
quiz.explanation: And He made cutting off kinship one of the major sins that anger Allah and His Messenger.

askTheBook: Who are one's kin?

days.title: From the Essentials of Good Manners: Forgiveness and Forbearance
days.question: How do I deal with someone who wrongs me or treats me unjustly?
days.principle: Muhammad ﷺ was sent to perfect noble character. Among the essentials of his manners are that a person keeps ties with whoever cuts him off, gives to whoever withholds from him, forgives whoever wrongs him, does good to whoever does him harm, honours those above him and is gentle with those below him, and avoids anger, except for Allah, as much as he can.

misconception.peopleSay: Answering harm with harm is what gets you your rights; forgiveness is weakness.
misconception.correct: Allah commanded the believers to be patient when angry, forbearing in the face of ignorance and forgiving when wronged. When a person does good to whoever wronged him, that good leads him to reconciliation and affection, until the other becomes like a close friend.

days.action: If someone upsets you today, try responding with what is better instead of responding in kind, and see what the verse says may happen.
lesson: The Prophet ﷺ was sent to perfect noble character; Allah praised him, saying "and indeed you are of a great moral character", and Aisha said his character was the Quran. He was not obscene, nor given to cursing or insulting, and he used to say that the best of you are those best in character. Anas served him for ten years, and he never said "uff" to him, or "why did you do that?" Allah commanded him to take what is easy, enjoin what is right and turn away from the ignorant; when 'Uyaynah behaved rudely with 'Umar, al-Hurr recited this verse, and 'Umar stopped at it and did not go beyond it. The Quran taught us to repel evil with what is better, so that an enemy becomes a close friend. Allah praised those who restrain their anger and pardon people.

quiz.question: Someone wronged you. What character does Allah love?
Your servant or an employee of yours made a mistake. What was the Prophet's ﷺ guidance?
What was the reference for the Prophet's ﷺ character?

askTheBook: What are the essentials of the Prophet's ﷺ manners?
What does "repel evil with what is better" mean?

days.title: From the Essentials of Good Manners: Respecting Elders and Self-Control in Anger
days.question: How do I treat elders and children? And how do I control myself when angry?
days.principle: Among the essentials of good manners are mercy to the young, respect for elders, and pardoning and forgiving people; the strong one is he who controls himself when angry; and the anger to beware of is worldly anger, while anger for Allah is in its proper place.

misconception.peopleSay: All anger is blameworthy in every situation.
misconception.correct: The anger to beware of is worldly anger; anger for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is in its proper place, and its owner is praised and rewarded for it. The Prophet ﷺ was patient with harm done to him personally, but when it concerned Allah, he carried out Allah's command with firmness.

days.action: If you get angry today, immediately say «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم», as the Prophet ﷺ guided.
lesson: Among the essentials of good manners are showing mercy to the young and knowing the honour of elders, and the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever does not do so is not one of us. The Companions were raised on this: Samurah ibn Jundub would stay silent as a boy out of respect for the elders, and Ibn 'Umar knew the answer to the palm tree riddle but was too shy to speak in front of Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Allah praised the believers who forgive when they are angry, and the Prophet ﷺ never took revenge for himself unless Allah's sanctities were violated. The Prophet ﷺ said the strong one is not the one who overpowers people, but the one who controls himself when angry, and he advised a man and repeated to him: do not become angry. But anger for Allah in its place is praiseworthy; the Prophet ﷺ became angry when he saw images in the house and when an imam prolonged the prayer for people. The remedy for anger is to say: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan.
days.quote: The reason anger leaves through seeking refuge, as scholars mention, is that when a person turns to Allah in that state, seeking refuge with Him from Shaytan, he remembers that there is no doer except Allah.

quiz.question: Who is truly strong?
options: The one who beats people in a fight
The one who controls himself when angry
The one with the strongest muscles
The one with the loudest voice

quiz.question: You became very angry. What is the Prophetic remedy?
options: Say: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan

quiz.question: Is all anger blameworthy?
options: No, anger for Allah in its place is praiseworthy; what is blameworthy is worldly anger
quiz.explanation: The anger to beware of here is worldly anger; anger for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is in its proper place, and its owner is praised and rewarded for it.

days.title: Good Things Are Lawful, Foul Things Unlawful, and the Religion Is Ease
days.question: Why did Allah forbid some things and allow others? And is the religion hard?
days.principle: Allah made good things lawful for His servants and foul things unlawful, and removed from them their burdens and the shackles that were upon them. He forbade nothing except for some immediate or eventual harm in it, and commanded nothing except for some immediate or eventual benefit in it.

misconception.peopleSay: Being strict in worship and burdening oneself beyond one's capacity is the height of religiousness.
misconception.correct: Excess and going beyond moderation in worship and other matters is blameworthy; what is praiseworthy is what one can keep up consistently. The Prophet ﷺ said: «إن الدين يسر، ولن يشاد الدين أحد إلا غلبه».

days.action: Choose one act of worship you can keep up consistently, even if small, rather than something big you do once and abandon, as the book says: what is praiseworthy is what one can keep up consistently.
lesson: The great rule is that Allah made good things lawful and foul things unlawful; He forbade nothing except because it contains harm, and commanded nothing except because it contains benefit. Ibn 'Abbas said that after the good lawful there is nothing but the foul unlawful. Another rule of the religion is the removal of hardship; Allah said He has not placed upon you any hardship in religion, and from this the scholars took the rule that hardship brings ease. The Prophet ﷺ said the religion is ease, and whoever is excessively strict in it will be overcome, exhausted and cut off. Aisha said the Prophet ﷺ was never given a choice between two things without choosing the easier, as long as it was not a sin. When a Bedouin urinated in the mosque, he told the Companions to leave him, for you were sent to make things easy and not to make them difficult.

quiz.question: Why did Allah forbid some things?
options: To make things hard for us
Because they contain immediate or eventual harm
quiz.explanation: He forbade nothing except for some immediate or eventual harm in it.

quiz.question: Someone is so strict with himself in worship that he can no longer keep going. Is this praiseworthy?
options: No, the religion is ease, and no one is excessively strict in it except that it overcomes him
quiz.explanation: Meaning: no one goes to extremes in religious deeds and abandons gentleness except that he becomes unable and is cut off, and so is overcome.

quiz.question: When choosing between two lawful matters, what was the Prophet's ﷺ guidance?
options: Choose the easier, as long as it is not a sin

askTheBook: Why did Allah make good things lawful and foul things unlawful?
What does "the religion is ease" mean?
What is the rule of removing hardship?

days.title: The Prohibition of Riba and Alcohol
days.question: What is the ruling on interest from usurious banks? And why is alcohol haram even in small amounts?
days.principle: Allah forbade riba, little or much, threatened those who deal in it with destruction and eternal punishment, and declared war on them from Allah and His Messenger. He forbade alcohol and cursed ten parties involved in it; every intoxicant is khamr and every khamr is haram.

misconception.peopleSay: This drink has a different name from khamr, so it isn't haram even if it intoxicates.
misconception.correct: Every intoxicant is khamr and every khamr is haram. Ibn 'Abbas was asked about al-badhiq and said: «سبق محمد ﷺ الباذق فما أسكر فهو حرام». So the rule prohibiting intoxicants includes it, and different names make no difference.

days.action: If you have any financial dealing with a suspicion of riba, review it today and ask the people of knowledge about its halal alternative.
lesson: At the end of Surat al-Baqarah, Allah addressed the believers strongly: give up riba, and if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. The book applies this to our reality and considers the interest on loans and deposits in usurious banks to be forbidden riba. The Prophet ﷺ counted consuming riba among the seven destructive sins, and cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who pays it, the one who writes it and its two witnesses, and said they are all the same. Then the book speaks about alcohol: Allah forbade it and called it filth from the work of Shaytan, and the Prophet ﷺ cursed ten parties involved in it. What counts is intoxication, not the name, so any intoxicating drink has the ruling of khamr. Even when a man said he made it for medicine, the Prophet ﷺ said it is not a medicine but a disease.
days.quote: Accordingly, all the increments that usurious banks pay or charge on loans and deposits are the forbidden riba that Allah and His Messenger have prohibited.

quiz.question: What is the ruling on the interest usurious banks pay on deposits?
options: Halal because it's a small percentage
quiz.explanation: Accordingly, all the increments that usurious banks pay or charge on loans and deposits are the forbidden riba that Allah and His Messenger have prohibited.

quiz.question: Someone works writing riba contracts but doesn't take interest himself. Is he sinning?
options: No, if he needs the job
Yes, the Prophet ﷺ also cursed the one who writes riba

quiz.question: A new drink not called "khamr" intoxicates. What is its ruling?
options: Halal because its name is different
Haram; every intoxicant is khamr and every khamr is haram

days.title: Carrion and Slaughtered Animals
days.question: What makes meat halal? And are the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book halal?
days.principle: Allah forbade carrion, blood, pork and what is dedicated to other than Allah. An animal is not lawful to eat except by proper slaughter, and its lawfulness requires that the slaughterer be a Muslim or one of the People of the Book, that he not deliberately omit saying Allah's name, and that he not dedicate his slaughter to other than Allah.

misconception.peopleSay: If I'm unsure whether Allah's name was said over meat coming from Muslims, I shouldn't eat it.
misconception.correct: Some people said to the Prophet ﷺ: people bring us meat and we do not know whether Allah's name was mentioned over it or not. He said: «سموا عليه أنتم وكلوه», and they were recent converts from disbelief.

days.action: If you slaughter or see someone slaughtering, remember that the Prophet ﷺ forbade slaughtering with teeth or nails because it tortures the animal, and make mercy to animals a habit.
lesson: Allah forbade carrion, blood, pork and what is dedicated to other than Allah, and an animal is not lawful except by proper slaughter. For an animal under control, slaughter is at the throat or the upper chest, cutting the oesophagus, the windpipe and the two jugular veins; for one not under control, such as a runaway camel, it is by a wound that takes its life. The slaughterer must be a Muslim or one of the People of the Book, and must not deliberately omit saying Allah's name. The Prophet ﷺ said: whatever makes the blood flow and Allah's name is mentioned over it, eat; and he forbade slaughtering with teeth or nails because it is torture. The food of the People of the Book is lawful for us, and Ibn 'Abbas said their food means their slaughtered animals. When people brought meat and did not know whether Allah's name had been said over it, the Prophet ﷺ told them to say Allah's name themselves and eat.
days.quote: Whatever has not been slaughtered according to the Shariah is carrion; that is why the default with meats and sexual relations is prohibition until lawfulness is established.

quiz.question: Meat comes from a land whose people are recent converts to Islam, and you don't know whether they said Allah's name over it. Do you eat it?
options: Say Allah's name yourself and eat

quiz.question: What is the ruling on animals slaughtered by the People of the Book?
options: Halal; their food means their slaughtered animals
quiz.explanation: Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from Ibn 'Abbas: their food means their slaughtered animals.

quiz.question: What is the ruling on slaughtering with teeth or nails?
options: Forbidden because it tortures the animal
quiz.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ forbade slaughtering with teeth and nails, because slaughtering with them tortures the animal.

days.title: Consuming People's Wealth Unjustly
days.question: Which financial dealings did Islam forbid to protect people's rights?
days.principle: Allah forbade bribery, cheating, deception, excessive uncertainty (gharar), artificial bidding (najsh), hoarding and the like: everything that leads to enmity and to consuming people's wealth unjustly.

misconception.peopleSay: A small thing I take from someone's right by swearing an oath is no problem.
misconception.correct: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «من اقتطع حق امرئ مسلم بيمينه فقد أوجب الله له النار وحرم عليه الجنة», and a man asked him: Even if it is something small? He said: «وإن كان قضيباً من أراك».

days.action: If you are selling or buying today, make sure you are clear about the item's defects and hide nothing, and remember: «من غش فليس مني».
lesson: The book forbids everything that leads to consuming people's wealth unjustly and creates enmity: bribery, cheating, deception, excessive uncertainty, artificial bidding and hoarding. The Prophet ﷺ found a man who had put the wet food underneath, and said to him: why didn't you put it on top so people could see it? Whoever cheats is not of me. He forbade sales involving excessive uncertainty, which is a great principle in trade covering the sale of unknown things and what cannot be handed over. Artificial bidding (najsh) is when someone raises the price of an item while not wanting to buy it, to trap someone else. Hoarding is buying goods at a time of high prices and holding them back so their price rises while people need them, and the Prophet ﷺ said no one hoards except a sinner. And whoever takes someone's right by a false oath, even a twig of arak, Allah has made the Fire obligatory for him.
days.quote: Najsh is raising the price of an item by someone who does not want to buy it, so that someone else falls into it.

quiz.question: A merchant put the good fruit on top and the bad fruit underneath. What is the ruling?
options: Cheating, and the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever cheats is not of me

quiz.question: Someone raises the price of an item at an auction while not wanting to buy it, so that someone else pays more. What is this?
quiz.explanation: Najsh is raising the price of an item by someone who does not want to buy it, so that someone else falls into it.

quiz.question: A merchant stockpiled goods people need during a crisis so their price would rise. What is the ruling?
quiz.explanation: Hoarding is buying goods at a time of high prices and holding them back so that their price rises while people need them.

days.title: Conclusion: Carry the Good to People
days.question: After learning all of this, what is my role with the people around me?
days.principle: Every Muslim should carry the call to this truth and a sincere desire for people's guidance, without distinguishing between anyone for reasons of race, region or religion.

misconception.peopleSay: Calling to Islam is the job of scholars and preachers only; it's none of my business.
misconception.correct: Every Muslim should carry the call to this truth and a sincere desire for people's guidance, and calling to Allah with clear insight is the way of the Prophet ﷺ and the way of everyone who follows him.

days.action: Choose one thing you learned in this journey that affected you, and share it today with someone, with wisdom and a kind word.
lesson: The book ends with a great responsibility on every Muslim: to carry this truth to people and wish from his heart for their guidance, without distinguishing between them because of origin, country or religion. Allah taught us the method of calling: with wisdom and good admonition, and if argument is needed, it is with gentleness and kindness. Even Musa and Harun were commanded by Allah to speak gently to Pharaoh, that perhaps he might remember. The Prophet ﷺ was extremely keen on people's guidance, to the point that Allah consoled him and told him not to destroy himself with grief over them. He told 'Ali that if Allah guides one man through you, it is better for you than red camels. And whoever calls to guidance gets the like of the reward of everyone who follows him, without anything being reduced from their rewards.
days.quote: So He commanded him to tell people that calling to Allah with clear insight, certainty and proof is his way and the way of everyone who follows him.

quiz.question: You invited someone to something good and he did it. What reward do you get?
options: The like of his reward, without anything reduced from his reward

quiz.question: You are calling a difficult, stubborn person. What should the approach be?
On what basis must calling to the religion be?
options: On clear insight, certainty and proof
quiz.explanation: So He commanded him to tell people that calling to Allah with clear insight, certainty and proof is his way and the way of everyone who follows him.
